fieldValues.title: Two more unhardened sibling-checkout resolvers found by grepping for the #874 shape
fieldValues.summary: discovery_conformance.rs's conformance_dir() and core_bundle_drift.rs's canonical-bundle check both resolved a sibling srs checkout without checking it was on master -- the same false-green trap srs-rust#874 named and PR #879 hardened once already, in rfc_035_parity.rs. Grepping tests/**/*.rs for CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR plus sibling-repo resolution after fixing the two found a third site, integration_tests.rs's srs_spec_repo_dir() Legacy fallback, which turned out to be dead code (shadowed by a higher-priority vendored-fixture check) rather than a live instance.
evidence: srs-rust#922 named discovery_conformance.rs's ext_discovery_fixture_scenarios specifically; grepping the same test tree surfaced core_bundle_drift.rs's canonical-srs check as an unhardened sibling too, unmentioned by the issue.

Reproduced live rather than hypothetically: this session's own srs sibling checkout sits on branch claude/trusting-tesla-94amp1 (its own designated feature branch, not master), and both tests silently passed against it with zero warning before the fix -- a genuine, unforced instance of the exact condition the guard exists to catch.

srs-rust PR #964 applies rfc_035_parity.rs::spec_repo()'s exact pattern (SRS_SPEC_DIR-first, loud panic naming the branch on a non-master sibling) to both sites, proved red-then-green against the live stale sibling and a fresh origin/master clone.
fieldValues.body: The pattern established once in PR #879 was documented there but not swept across the rest of the test tree at the time -- each occurrence has so far been found by a human or agent tripping over it (or, per srs-rust#921's Parks note, noticing it in passing) rather than by a repo-wide check. Nothing today greps for a bare CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR-plus-sibling-walk shape and flags it as needing the SRS_SPEC_DIR/branch-check treatment; the class is closed instance-by-instance, not structurally. A registered check for this shape (or a shared test-helper crate exposing the hardened resolver, so new tests default to safe instead of opting in) would prevent a fourth occurrence rather than relying on the next grep.
